tb21_profile.skill: Read a slow SQL query, work out why it is slow (correlated subqueries re-evaluated per row), and rewrite it with CTEs/window functions so it is materially faster while returning byte-identical rows, with no schema or index changes allowed
tb21_profile.domain: SQLite dialect, relational query semantics and the query planner: joins, correlated subqueries, aggregates, window functions, EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN
tb21_profile.task_form: optimise-for-a-budget under an exact-equivalence constraint; the deliverable is one SQL statement whose output must hash-match the original and whose runtime is benchmarked over repeated runs

searches: tools.py search all 'window function|correlated subquer|common table expression|\bCTE\b|OVER \(PARTITION' -n 30
tools.py search all 'EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN|query plan|rewrite the query|optimize.{0,30}(query|SQL)' -n 30
tools.py search rts 'SQL quer|SELECT .*FROM|sqlite3|JOIN |GROUP BY|CREATE INDEX|optimiz.{0,30}quer' -n 35

TMax-15K.reason: Optimize a slow SQLite query so it returns the exact same rows and columns, verified against a measured 20x speedup baseline. Same task, same constraints.
Replace a naive, unusably slow report with a single query using complex joins and window functions that emits the exact same columns and data.
Rewrite an N+1 query pattern into one CTE/window-function query and meet a hard 2.5 second wall-clock budget. Exactly the rewrite class this task needs.
Push Python-side row loops into a single SQLite query using OVER/PARTITION BY to compute a moving average, with the output unchanged.
Collapse nested loops and hundreds of individual queries into one efficient parameterized SQL query with window functions for ranking.
Reverse-engineer an undocumented SQLite schema, rewrite the slow query with exact ordering/tie-breaking and pagination, and export its EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN.
Read EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for a slow SQLite query and turn every SCAN TABLE into SEARCH TABLE while the query's output stays fixed.
A recursive CTE has an implicit cross join from a missing join condition, exploding the plan and the result set; diagnose from the plan and fix the SQL.
Speed up a set of slow SQLite graph queries in a pipeline that is running unacceptably slowly; same diagnose-then-make-it-fast loop.
Design covering indexes for a specific analytical query, capture its EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and run it; planner-directed tuning, but via indexes not rewriting.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Write a three-table join with exact filter predicates and column list, then cross-check the full output against an expected result. Exact-output SQL authoring.
Add an index on a join/filter column and write an aggregate SQL query that checks debits equal credits; indexing plus set-level SQL reasoning.
Inner join two tables then group by a key and compute count, sum and average per group. The relational-algebra core of the query being rewritten.
Author windowed join queries to a written contract and then append a measured PERF elapsed-time line. SQL plus an explicit timing deliverable.
A windowed join plus an anti-join filter for rows with no match; reasoning about join semantics and which rows survive.
Apply SQL files in order to build a SQLite database then report per-account balances and transaction counts. Aggregate queries over a real schema.
Verify computed summary counts against the source database with sqlite3 and log mismatches; the same must-match-the-original discipline.
Discover the real stream and column definitions from the workspace, then write join queries against them; schema-discovery before query writing.
Time an operation and issue a pass/fail verdict against a threshold read from a contract. Optimise-to-a-budget genre, wrong domain entirely.
Run a SELECT under a restricted role, emit exact CSV output, and validate the schema against declared rules; precision about SQL output format.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Run SELECTs with JSON-path filters against a table and capture EXPLAIN output showing index usage. Reading a query plan in the same engine family.
Write a three-table join with two equality predicates returning a specific column list. Exact-output relational query authoring.
Author a windowed LEFT JOIN and a follow-up filter over streams; window and outer-join semantics, which the rewrite must preserve.
Aggregate per key then left-join so unmatched groups survive with nulls. The classic aggregate-then-join rewrite of a correlated subquery.
Write and run a SQL script exercising JSONB operators and functions; dialect-specific SQL authoring with the output captured verbatim.
Convert line-delimited JSON into a SQLite table; working directly with a SQLite database file, but no query-shape reasoning.
Initialise a pgbench dataset and verify replication; database benchmarking machinery, adjacent to measuring a query's cost.
Execute a SELECT and produce exactly the expected CSV including the header row; precision about query output format.
Run a benchmarking pipeline that generates inputs, times executions and computes averages. Same measure-then-compare-runtimes genre, no SQL.
Benchmark six implementations of the same program and compare their execution speeds; runtime comparison under a fixed workload.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: The optimizer no longer eliminates and inlines CTEs correctly; deciding when a CTE can be folded without changing results is this task's central judgement.
eliminate_joins breaks on ordinary join conditions; removing work from a query while keeping its result set identical is exactly the TB constraint.
Optimizer hint comments are stripped when they must be preserved; understanding which comment text is semantically load-bearing to the planner.
LAG/LEAD default arguments are dropped during SQL generation; precise window-function semantics, the construct the rewrite is supposed to introduce.
SELECT expressions containing ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) are split into the wrong identifiers; parsing window expressions correctly inside a projection.
Parenthesised subqueries and joins are mis-structured by the aligned formatter; requires tracking subquery nesting, the thing being un-nested here.
A query builder drops clauses, producing SQL that no longer means what was asked; composing a valid statement clause by clause.
Nested CASE inside BEGIN is split into several statements; statement-boundary reasoning, relevant to emitting one single terminated query.
Date arithmetic fails to transpile in one dialect; dialect-specific SQL generation, which the sqlite-syntax-only requirement also hinges on.
The tokenizer loses comments attached to SQL tokens; low-level SQL lexing in the same ecosystem, little transfer to rewriting for speed.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: A scalar subquery used inside a function is not detected; requires reading exactly where a correlated subquery sits in a statement.
Make a UNION result usable as a subquery so an aggregate can run over it; composing nested SELECTs that stay semantically correct.
Support selecting from several tables and derived subqueries at once; the FROM-list and derived-table structure a rewrite reorganises.
Keyset pagination breaks on a column type; reasoning about ordering keys and comparison predicates in generated SQL.
A SQL formatter loses comments when round-tripping a model through its AST; fidelity of a transformed statement to the original.
A statement fails to parse because dialect and templater configuration is not honoured; dialect sensitivity, as the sqlite-only requirement demands.
A leading comment makes a SQL definition file fail to load; comment placement changing how a statement parses.
Generalize an API that only works against a built sqlite database; querying a SQLite file as the system of record.
A SQLite connector breaks when several tables are wired up; plumbing around querying a SQLite file, no query-shape reasoning.
A sqlite3 OperationalError because the database directory is missing; touches SQLite only as a storage dependency.

final_top10.reason: Optimize a slow SQLite query to return the exact same rows and columns, graded on a measured speedup against the original. Same task, same constraints.
Replace an unusably slow naive report with one query using complex joins and window functions that emits the exact same columns and data.
Rewrite an N+1 query pattern into a single CTE/window-function query under a hard wall-clock budget. Precisely the rewrite class this task needs.
Push per-row Python work into one SQLite query using OVER/PARTITION BY for a moving average, with identical output required.
Collapse nested loops and hundreds of round-trips into one efficient SQL query using window functions for ranking.
Reverse-engineer the schema, rewrite the slow query with exact ordering, tie-breaking and pagination, and export its EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN.
CTE elimination and inlining in a SQL optimizer stops working; when a CTE may be folded without changing results is this task's central judgement.
Read EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for a slow SQLite query and drive every SCAN TABLE to SEARCH TABLE while the query's own output is held fixed.
A recursive CTE's missing join condition creates an implicit cross join that blows up the plan; diagnose from the plan and correct the SQL.
A join-elimination optimizer rule breaks; removing work from a query while its result set stays identical is exactly the TB2.1 constraint.

notes: TMax is very strong here - it contains a whole family of 'this SQLite query is too slow, make it fast and keep the output identical' tasks - so final_top10 is mostly TMax plus the two sqlglot optimizer-rule bugs, which are the only documents in the entire pool that reason directly about when a CTE or a join can be removed without changing results. One judgement call worth flagging: the TB2.1 task forbids touching the database, so pure-rewrite tasks (task_000576, task_000012, task_000130) transfer better than index-tuning tasks, and I ranked them above the otherwise-excellent index/EXPLAIN tasks for that reason; task_004065 still tops the list because it allows either and grades on a measured speedup with exact-output equivalence. SWE-Smith reduces to sqlglot and sqlparse, the pool's only SQL-engine repositories; they lose on task_form as the spec predicts but carry real domain and skill weight. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is weak: its 733 hits for SQL-ish terms are dominated by two collision families - 'join' matching Kubernetes/Teleport cluster join tokens and the KSQL stream-join template repeated dozens of times - and it has no query-optimization task at all, so its best entries are ordinary join/group-by authoring scored at 3. TerminalWorld likewise has no SQL optimization task; tw_654258 (EXPLAIN showing index usage) is the only genuine planner-reading item and the tail is benchmark-a-program tasks chosen for task_form alone.
